findings.changed_text: every training row is added twice
findings.problem: Mirror augmentation now puts an exact mirrored twin of every training image into the training data, but the design never says where the doubling sits relative to the splits. Features (with the augmentation) are listed before the Split step, and GridSearchCV, the 5-fold cross_val_score, the validation split from train_test_split(stratify=y) and the learning curve all run inside the training set. If the doubled rows are split at random, an image lands in one fold and its twin lands in another. The twin has identical finger-extension ratios (distances do not change under a mirror) and differs only in the flipped x coordinates. Cross-validation scores, the learning curve and the GridSearchCV choice of C, gamma and tree depth are then inflated and favour memorising. This is the near-duplicate leakage the same section promises to explain and that Part 2 avoids with GroupKFold. The official 372-image test set is untouched, so the 95% criterion stays honest, but the CV, learning-curve and tuning figures shown to the professor would not be.
findings.remedy: Give each image and its mirror the same group id and run GridSearchCV, cross_val_score, the validation split and the learning curve with GroupKFold or GroupShuffleSplit on that id (as Part 2 does), or augment only inside each training fold and for the final fit. State the chosen rule in the Features or Split bullets so the notebook and the viva guide explain it.

findings.problem: Parity check 2 now sends 20 images in two variants (40 pushes), but its pass rule is still written for one: 'at least 19 of 20' is not tied to a variant or restated as 38 of 40. A left-right flipped copy has landmarks mirrored about the image centre, so compared raw with the unflipped CSV row it differs by far more than the 0.02 limit; the text does not say the landmarks are un-flipped, or the comparison made on a mirror-invariant feature, first. It also does not say whether the live decode path applies its own selfie flip (Datasets > Mirror convention; the shared-helpers bullet says only 'the image decode and mirroring'). If it does, the as-is copy is flipped once and the flipped copy twice, and only one of them can match the unflipped CSV landmarks.
findings.remedy: Say where the selfie flip is applied (browser or Python), define the flipped-copy comparison (un-flip the landmarks before the 0.02 check, or compare the predicted label and the mirror-invariant ratios), and state the count rule per variant (for example at least 19 of 20 for each).

findings.changed_text: Webcam frames are flipped horizontally before detection

The statement that MediaPipe's handedness label assumes a mirrored input is also given without a source; I could not confirm it for the HandLandmarker task from the document. CGI images are fed unflipped, so their stored label can look inverted in any exploration plot.
findings.remedy: Drop the handedness columns and the webcam flip (a CSS-mirrored preview still gives the selfie look), or keep them with a named exploration use, a citation or a spike check for the pinned HandLandmarker, and a note that CGI labels are for an unflipped image.

findings.changed_text: so a left hand and a right hand give the same prediction

The only offline evidence is 20 flipped images in parity check 2, a label-agreement check, and the official 372-image test set is not said to be scored mirrored, so the first measurement of left-hand accuracy is the spike or the live test with people.
findings.remedy: Soften the sentence and report the best model's accuracy on the official test set both as-is and mirrored (the 95% criterion applying to both), or average the model's probabilities over a frame and its mirror at prediction time.
